annual.note: total return by calendar year (Chartrow; 2026 to 23 Oct)

backbone: Food and grocery deliveries: 53% of revenue, +21%.
Financial services (loans, payments, digital banks): 13% but growing 59%; loan book $2.3bn, tripled in a year.
54m monthly users; $6.5bn of on-demand orders a quarter (+21%).
bear: Spending cash on deals while fintech still loses money ($15m adj. EBITDA loss in Q2).
Credit risk from a loan book growing about 200% a year.
Regulation: Indonesian commission caps, a Vietnam competition inquiry, GoTo merger stalled on monopoly concerns.
GAAP free cash flow negative over the last 12 months (-$160m).
bull: $4.5bn net cash (40% of its market value) and a $750m buyback.
CEO bought about $30m of shares at ~$2.90 in September.
All 24 analysts on StockAnalysis rate it Buy or Strong Buy.
check: Market cap $11.4bn minus net cash $4.5bn = EV $6.9bn; divided by the 2026 adj. EBITDA midpoint ($0.73bn) = 9.4x. Targets imply about +100%, but four were cut this month and TipRanks still uses a $3.58 price, so treat the average as optimistic.

events.text: Q3 2026 results (date per StockAnalysis/Nasdaq, not yet confirmed by Grab)

history_notes: Biggest fall: -86.5% from its Nov 2021 high ($17.06) to Oct 2022, and it has never recovered; still about 83% below that peak. Beta 0.91.
Results days swing it: +12.6% intraday on a beat (12 Nov 2024), about -12% premarket on weak guidance (20 Feb 2025).
22 Sep 2026: +8.9% when the CEO bought about $30m of shares at a 3-year low.
name: Grab Holdings
oneliner: Southeast Asia's super-app: food delivery, ride-hailing and digital lending. Down 55% from its high and near a 3-year low.
range_note: Average target $5.58 (StockAnalysis); MarketBeat $6.01, TipRanks $5.20. Every October change was a cut, though all kept Buy ratings.

targets.note: MarketBeat average $6.01, TipRanks $5.20. Every October change was a cut, all keeping Buy.

verdict: Cheapest in 3 years with a big cash pile, but already your largest single share (15% of the ISA). Hold; don't add until the 2 Nov results show the Atome deal and incentives are under control.

why_down.text: Q2 profit flattered by a one-off Superbank gain; incentives rose to 10.9% of orders.
Agreed to buy 60% of lender Atome for $1.49bn; shares fell 7.5% in four days.
Barclays, Citi, Maybank and BofA cut targets; back near the $2.74 low.
